visual_goal: Show the lifecycle of a finding: machine detections and inspector entries both start unconfirmed, only confirmed findings go on, disputes can uphold or overturn, and a repair supersedes a finding instead of deleting it.
prompt: A simple state map of six rounded tiles on a light background. Left side, stacked: a blue tile with a small camera-lens icon labeled 'Detected by model' at the upper left and a blue tile with a small clipboard icon labeled 'Recorded by inspector' at the lower left. Center: a large green tile labeled 'Confirmed'. Directly right of 'Confirmed', on the same row: an orange tile labeled 'Disputed'. Top, above the gap between 'Confirmed' and 'Disputed': a grey tile labeled 'Rejected'. Bottom center, directly below 'Confirmed': a teal tile with a small wrench icon labeled 'Superseded by repair'. Exactly seven arrows, each label written once: one from 'Detected by model' right into 'Confirmed' labeled 'reviewer accepts'; one from 'Detected by model' along the top into 'Rejected' labeled 'reflection, dirt, duplicate'; one from 'Recorded by inspector' right into 'Confirmed' labeled 'photo attached, reviewed'; between 'Confirmed' and 'Disputed' two parallel horizontal arrows: the upper one pointing right from 'Confirmed' to 'Disputed' labeled 'contests', the lower one pointing left from 'Disputed' back to 'Confirmed' labeled 'upheld'; one from 'Disputed' up into 'Rejected' labeled 'overturned'; one from 'Confirmed' straight down into 'Superseded by repair' labeled 'repair order closed'.
alt: Detected-by-model and recorded-by-inspector findings move to Confirmed or Rejected; confirmed findings can be disputed and upheld or overturned, or superseded by a repair.

visual_goal: Show Gauge storing evidence once and deriving every view from confirmed findings, with consumers referencing reports and estimates and sending recon actuals and disputes back.
prompt: A left-to-right architecture illustration. Far left: a phone and a drive-through camera arch together in one box labeled 'Inspect and scanners'. Next: a database cylinder with a small padlock labeled 'Evidence store'. Above-right of it: a box with a scanning-eye icon labeled 'Detection gateway'. Center: a large box with a reviewer checklist icon labeled 'Findings and review'. Right of center, stacked: a box labeled 'Rubric engine' on top and a box with a calculator icon labeled 'Estimating' below. Further right: a box with an outgoing-plug icon labeled 'Condition API'. Far right: a group of four generic screens labeled 'Consumers'. Exactly ten arrows: one from 'Inspect and scanners' to 'Evidence store' labeled 'observations with hashes'; one from 'Evidence store' up to 'Detection gateway'; one from 'Detection gateway' to 'Findings and review' labeled 'unconfirmed findings'; one long arrow from 'Inspect and scanners' along the bottom into 'Findings and review' labeled 'inspector findings'; one from 'Findings and review' to 'Rubric engine' and one from 'Findings and review' to 'Estimating', both in green labeled 'confirmed findings' once; one from 'Rubric engine' to 'Condition API' labeled 'grade, charge, report'; one from 'Estimating' to 'Condition API' labeled 'estimates'; one from 'Condition API' to 'Consumers'; one curved orange return arrow over the top from 'Consumers' back to 'Findings and review' labeled 'recon actuals, disputes'.
alt: Inspect and scanners send hashed observations to the evidence store; detections and inspector findings meet in findings and review; confirmed findings feed the rubric engine and estimating, which serve the condition API to consumers, who return recon actuals and disputes.

visual_goal: Show that condition enters the buying decision through two separate paths, reconditionable findings via the recon estimate and residual findings via the valuation, with actual costs returning to calibrate the rate card.
prompt: A top-to-bottom flow illustration with six boxes. Top center: a stack of plain cards labeled 'Confirmed findings'. One arrow down into an orange diamond labeled 'Reconditionable or residual'. From the diamond two arrows: one down-left labeled 'reconditionable' into a blue box labeled 'Recon estimate', and one down-right labeled 'residual' into a blue box labeled 'Condition line'. From both boxes one arrow each converging down into a green box labeled 'Maximum purchase price' at the bottom center. Far left, level with 'Recon estimate': a box with a small bar-chart icon labeled 'Recon variance'. One single-headed teal arrow pointing from 'Recon variance' right into 'Recon estimate', labeled 'calibrate'; it has an arrowhead only at the 'Recon estimate' end. Icons contain no words, letters or symbols.
alt: Confirmed findings split into reconditionable (recon estimate) and residual (condition line); both feed the maximum purchase price, and approved recon lines produce actuals and variance that calibrate the recon estimate.
